title: Did Archimedes build a death ray?
summary: Hosts open with banter about genius, reproduction and Jeffrey Sachs, then profile Archimedes: his life in Syracuse, pi calculation, the bathtub discovery of displacement and the gold crown story of King Hiero II, his war machines during the Roman siege of Syracuse (the iron claw), and his reported death ray of mirrors. They discuss the 2005 MIT replica, a 2011 Eric Jacques Maine build, MythBusters' attempts, a Greek researcher's fifty-soldier test, and reasons the death ray was likely fictional. A listener letter about Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (from George in Brighton, UK) closes the episode. Ad reads bookend the episode.

segments.title: Opening banter and genius talk
segments.summary: Hosts joke about recent episodes, Jeffrey Sachs's idea that more people means more geniuses, and Office Space. They transition to Archimedes as an early genius.

segments.title: Archimedes' life and pi
segments.summary: Archimedes is introduced as a mathematician, physicist and engineer born around 287 BC in Syracuse, Sicily. His work on calculating pi and proofs ahead of calculus is discussed.

segments.title: Gold crown and principle of displacement
segments.summary: Hiero II asks Archimedes to test whether a crown made by a goldsmith is pure gold. Archimedes discovers displacement while bathing and tests the crown by comparing water displacement with a pure gold bar of equal weight. The hosts note the story's ending is uncertain.

segments.title: Archimedes' inventions and the Siege of Syracuse
segments.summary: Hosts discuss Archimedes as a modifier of existing inventions such as the catapult and water screw. Syracuse allied with Rome, then switched to Carthage, and Marcellus besieged the city for two years. Archimedes' war machines were used against the Romans, including the iron claw that lifted and capsized ships.

segments.title: Archimedes' death ray and burning mirrors
segments.summary: Hosts describe the death ray legend, noting Galen mentions ships burned remotely about 350 years later and Anthemius of Tralles in the 5th century suggested mirrors. They cover the MIT replica, Eric Jacques Maine's satellite-dish build, MythBusters' two busted verdicts, and a Greek researcher who set rowboats on fire with about fifty soldiers holding mirrors. They list reasons it likely did not exist.

segments.title: Closing banter and Grace Jones
segments.summary: Hosts ask whether a modern military has tried sun-based weapons, reference a Bond film, and briefly discuss Grace Jones. They point listeners to the website for more on Archimedes.

segments.title: Listener mail: Ehlers-Danlos syndrome
segments.summary: George from Brighton, UK writes about living with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome, which has caused many joint dislocations, and asks for an episode on it. The hosts respond and give social media and contact info, followed by an ad line.
